issues.description: The problem statement requires Farm to use a List<Animal> and explicitly instructs initializing an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor, but the solution implementation uses a Set<Animal> with a HashSet. This mismatch in the collection type (List/ArrayList vs Set/HashSet) is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which collection type to use and how to implement/getters/setters for the animals attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution and template with the problem statement: change the Farm implementation to use List<Animal> and initialize it as an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor (and update getter/setter signatures accordingly), or update the problem statement to accept Set/HashSet if that collection type is intended.

issues.description: The problem UML and description indicate a private helper method singFarmSongVerse should accept an Animal parameter (singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal): void), but the template's Farm.java declares singFarmSongVerse without a parameter (the Animal parameter is commented out). This method signature mismatch in the template prevents direct use of the helper with an Animal and can confuse students about the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's singFarmSongVerse signature to accept an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) and adjust its body to use the provided animal (e.g., animal.getClass().getSimpleName(), animal.messageOnFeed()). This will match the UML/specification and the solution reference.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly describes the Farm's collection of animals as a List and instructs students to initialize an ArrayList in the no-argument constructor (concept: collection-of-animals). The reference solution, however, declares the attribute as a Set<Animal> and initializes a HashSet. This names two different collection implementations (ArrayList vs. HashSet) for the same conceptual entity and deviates from the problem instructions, creating a mapping confusion for students who are told to use ArrayList but see a HashSet in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent with the problem statement: change the solution's Farm attribute to use List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() (and adjust import/signatures accordingly). Alternatively, update the problem statement to accept Set/HashSet explicitly if that is the intended design.
